Dear Colleague,

I saw Karen Mitchell, a 76-year-old female, in consultation on December 6, 2025. Ms. Mitchell was referred for a review of her medical history, particularly her history of colon cancer, stage I, which was diagnosed approximately 17.1 years ago on October 20, 2007.

Upon review of her medical history, Ms. Mitchell underwent treatment for colon cancer, stage I, and has been in a controlled status for several years now. The treatment included surgical resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. Since her treatment, Ms. Mitchell has remained under close surveillance with regular follow-ups, and there have been no signs of recurrence. 

During her last visit on December 6, 2025, Ms. Mitchell reported no new symptoms or complaints. She mentioned occasional mild abdominal discomfort, which she attributed to her diet, and some fatigue that she has experiencing off and on. Vital signs during this visit showed a blood pressure of mmHg and a weight of 165 pounds, which are within acceptable limits. 

On examination, Ms. Mitchell appeared well. Her general physical exam was unremarkable, with no palpable masses or lymphadenopathy. Her cardiovascular and respiratory exams were normal. Abdominal exam revealed mild distension but no tenderness or rebound. Extremities showed no edema, and her exam was intact.

Laboratory results from the latest follow-up were reviewed. Her complete blood count, liver function tests, and tumor markers (CEA) were all within normal limits. Colonoscopy performed six months ago revealed no evidence of recurrent disease.

Given her stable condition and the absence of any new findings, I continue to recommend Ms. Mitchell remain under regular surveillance. She should continue her routine follow-ups, which include periodic colonoscopies, imaging, and blood tests as appropriate.

Social history reveals that Ms. Mitchell consumes approximately 12 alcoholic drinks per week, which is within moderate limits. There is no of tobacco use. Her family history is non-contributory with no significant cancer history.

In summary, Ms. Mitchell's colon cancer, stage I, remains controlled with no evidence of recurrence. She continues to do well with no new symptoms. Regular follow-ups and surveillance are advised to ensure continued control of her condition.

Thank you for referring Ms. Mitchell to our care. Please do not hesitate to contact us should there be any further concerns or additional information needed.

Sincerely,
